items.claim: CEO announces the company is raising its full-year 2025 outlook to approximately 14% revenue growth and 18% EPS growth.
items.quote: raising our full year outlook to approximately 14%
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CFO gives Q4 2025 revenue guidance range.
items.quote: revenue in the range of $1.405 billion to $1.435 billion
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CFO gives updated full-year 2025 revenue guidance range.
items.quote: revenue in the range of $5.262 billion and $5.292 billion
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CFO explicitly declines to give FY2026 guidance on this call, deferring to a later date.
items.quote: we won't guide FY '26 today
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CFO gives updated full-year 2025 GAAP operating margin guidance range.
items.quote: GAAP operating margin in the range of 27.9% to 28.9%.
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CFO states Q3 2025 actual GAAP operating margin.
items.quote: GAAP operating margin was 31.8%
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CFO explains Q4 opex is partly offset by new expenses from recently closed acquisitions.
items.quote: offset a little in Q4 by some new expenses
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: Analyst asks how Cadence's strong IP growth squares with a competitor's publicly expressed concerns about its own IP business.
items.quote: because your competitor expressed
items.speaker: Vivek Arya (Analyst, BofA Securities)

items.claim: CEO argues Cadence's IP business is more profitable than the general IP industry, differentiating it from competitors.
items.quote: I think it's much more profitable
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CEO cites Q3 expansion of the Samsung partnership across core EDA and system software.
items.quote: we meaningfully expanded our partnership with Samsung
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CEO cites deepened collaboration with OpenAI on the Palladium emulation platform in Q3.
items.quote: We deepened our overall collaboration with OpenAI
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CEO cites Samsung's SF2 tape-out using Cadence Cerebrus AI Studio as a customer productivity win.
items.quote: Samsung U.S. taped out a SF2 design using Cadence Cerebrus
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CEO cites customer-reported verification throughput gains from Verisium SimAI, highlighted by NVIDIA, Samsung and Qualcomm at CadenceLIVE India.
items.quote: 5x to 10x improvement in verification throughput
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CFO states the 2025 outlook assumes today's export control regulations remain substantially similar for the rest of the year.
items.quote: export control regulations that exist today remain
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: When asked about China tariff-related risk to guidance, CFO says reports suggest geopolitical tensions are lower than commonly expected.
items.quote: geopolitical tensions are lower than people expect
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CFO states Q3 2025 share repurchase amount.
items.quote: we used $200 million to repurchase Cadence shares
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CEO confirms the definitive agreement to acquire Hexagon's D&E business, including its MSC Software unit.
items.quote: signed a definitive agreement to acquire Hexagon's D&E
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CFO reiterates the 2025 outlook includes using at least 50% of annual free cash flow for buybacks.
items.quote: our annual free cash flow to repurchase Cadence shares
items.speaker: John Wall (CFO)

items.claim: CEO states the combined SD&A business run rate should cross $1 billion in 2026 once the Hexagon acquisition closes.
items.quote: $1 billion in 2026 if the acquisition closes.
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

items.claim: CEO states he would be surprised if the IP business does not grow faster than the corporate average given its profitability profile.
items.quote: our IP business does not grow better than Cadence average
items.speaker: Anirudh Devgan (CEO)

qa_flags.question: Joseph Quatrochi (Wells Fargo) asked why Q3 opex came in better than expected but Q4 opex looks worse, and whether that relates to Artisan deal timing.
qa_flags.response_pattern: John Wall's first answer discussed broad-based execution and demand across product categories without addressing the opex timing question; the analyst had to re-ask ('I guess maybe just a question on the OpEx...') and John Wall asked him to repeat the question before giving a specific answer.

qa_flags.question: Charles Shi / Yu Shi (Needham) asked directly whether hardware growth could decelerate in year 3 of the current Z3/X3 upgrade cycle, as it did in year 3 of the prior Z2/X2 cycle.
qa_flags.response_pattern: John Wall responded 'We're trying to unpack it' and pivoted to general commentary on backlog, pipeline strength and revenue-curve shape across quarters, without directly confirming or denying a year-3 deceleration comparable to the prior cycle.
